messages:
maria_prod: Heads-up — multiple support tickets reporting intermittent 5xx and long tail timeouts hitting hosted inference in eu-west-1. Customers see bursty 502/504s and elevated p95/p99 latency for gen endpoints. I can repro from our synthetic tests too.

support_sam: Ticket IDs: SUP-3291, SUP-3293. Customers noticed errors starting ~15m ago, spikes every ~30-90s. They say requests sometimes succeed if retried.

oncall-bot: Alert: Hostgroup eu-west-1-prod-api crossed 500 errors threshold (5m). Incident channel: #incidents.

maria_prod: Adding neteng and infra. @leo_neteng @ivan_infra can you grab flow logs and a quick mtr/traceroute from our edge nodes to the affected AZs?

leo_neteng: Looking. Initial mtr from edge-pop-eu1 to gw-eu1-azb shows packet loss starting after transit hop. Short excerpt: 
```
  1  10.0.8.1  0.3%  0.3%  0.3%  1ms
  2  203.0.113.45  0.0%  0.0%  0.0%  8ms
  3  * * *  (flapping) 30-40% loss
  4  198.51.100.23  0.0%  0.0%  0.0%  14ms
```
Looks like microbursts/loss on hop 3 which is our transit provider.

ivan_infra: Flow logs + gw counters corroborate — TX/RX retransmits rise in eu-west-1 AZ-B around the same windows. CPU and memory on runtime nodes look fine.

ben_platform: Any recent routing changes or peering churn? deploy-bot, did we deploy any edge config or route changes?

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15T08:45:27 UTC: edge-route-policy-update rolled to 10% in eu-regions. No gateway config changes to AZ-B.

leo_neteng: I pulled BGP update logs from transit provider (EdgeWave). They show intermittent AS path prepends and withdraw/reannounce for a specific prefix covering eu-west-1 egress. Times align with error spikes. Could be provider instability or a flapping circuit.

maria_prod: Customers asking for ETA and if we can fail traffic to another AZ. Can we do an AZ failover on hosted inference?

ivan_infra: We have cross-zone routing but rolling failover is non-trivial mid-traffic — we can route new requests to eu-west-1 AZ-A (healthy) by adjusting smart-routing policy for the model route. That will reduce capacity in AZ-B but should avoid the transit path. I can start a canary to shift 40% of traffic in 5 minutes. Need approval.

support_sam: Please proceed, customers are requesting mitigation. Flagging for credits if this drags on.

leo_neteng: Quick mitigation alternatives: 1) Adjust BGP community to prefer alternate transit (requires provider cooperation) 2) Apply route pinning to send traffic via eu-west-1 AZ-A 3) Short term: increase TCP retransmit timeouts / MSS clamping at our edge to reduce stalls (not ideal).

maria_prod: Do 2 + 1 in parallel. Start shifting traffic now and open contact with EdgeWave NOC. Ivan — initiate the routing policy shift. Leo — open ticket with EdgeWave and ask for circuit check and if they saw micro-restarts.

ivan_infra: Kicking off smart-routing change. Command snippets used: 
```
# set route policy for model:resp
redwood route update --model gpt-open-13b --region eu-west-1 --policy smart-routing --weights az-a=60,az-b=40 --reason "incident mitigation"
```
Applying canary: 10% -> 40% over 5m. Monitoring token-level error rate and p99 latency.

leo_neteng: EdgeWave NOC replied: "we see intermittent link-level CRC errors on one provisioning circuit between POP-3 and transit-aggregator; techs are on-site replacing optics. ETA 45 minutes." They also said BGP flaps were likely caused by link instability.

maria_prod: Good. Ivan — any signs the canary reduced customer errors?

ivan_infra: Early signal: error-rate for the model route dropped ~65% for requests routed to AZ-A. Overall cluster 5xx decreased from 3.8% to 1.1% in 12m. p99 latency improved from 1.2s -> 0.38s for canary traffic.

ben_platform: Noted: we did have a recent edge-route-policy-update deploy — rolling back to previous policy would have forced stricter pinning and might have hidden this. But current mitigation looks ok.

maria_prod: Ok continue shift to 80/20 for next 10m if metrics keep improving. Also enable extra retry logic on the gateway (idempotent-safe retriers) for 502/504s for 60s window.

ivan_infra: Increasing routing weight to az-a=80 az-b=20 now. Enabling gateway retriers (2 tries, 300ms backoff) for affected routes.

leo_neteng: EdgeWave confirmed optics replaced. They saw no BGP withdraws after replacement. We'll keep monitoring for 30m before fully restoring weights.

support_sam: Let support/customer success know: customers SUP-3291/SUP-3293 notified of temporary routing and ETA. Asked if they want credits; we'll evaluate after post-incident.

maria_prod: Postmortem action items: - Add synthetic probes that check downstream path diversity (detect transit micro-loss) - Add automatic failover policy trigger for sustained retransmit spikes on gw counters - Document runbook for provider NOC contact and BGP community tweaks - Re-run traffic shaping test in eu-west-1 once stable.

oncall-bot: Incident status -> mitigation in progress. Errors decreased; provider repair in progress.

maria_prod: Thanks team. I'll keep this thread as the incident record. If errors return or EdgeWave reports more flaps, we'll escalate to execs.

deploy-bot: Rollout note: route policy change performed by ivan_infra at 2026-03-15T09:12:00Z.

ivan_infra: Marking for follow-up: will post logs (flow + tcpdump snippets) to the incident attach once noise subsides.

ben_platform: Filing post-incident ticket to evaluate default retry policy and canary thresholds.

maria_prod: Closing for now — monitoring until EdgeWave confirms stable. Will file postmortem in 24h. :white_check_mark:
